label: Problem set 17
title: Problem set 17: Spectroelectrochemistry and photoelectrochemistry
summary: Practice with coupled optical and light-driven methods: Beer-Lambert analysis, band gaps and threshold wavelengths, thin-layer coulometry and electrogenerated chemiluminescence.

intro.text: Spectroelectrochemistry couples the cell to a spectrometer, so products are identified while they form; the Beer-Lambert law A = eps c l links absorbance to concentration.

Photoelectrochemistry uses light to create charge carriers. The band gap follows Eg(eV) = 1240/lambda(nm), and light below the threshold wavelength cannot drive the reaction. Electrogenerated chemiluminescence emits light from an excited state made electrochemically.

sections.title: Hint sheet: optical and photoelectrochemical relations
sections.summary: Practice with coupled optical and light-driven methods: Beer-Lambert analysis, band gaps and threshold wavelengths, thin-layer coulometry and electrogenerated chemiluminescence.

blocks.text: Spectroelectrochemistry couples the cell to a spectrometer, so products are identified while they form; the Beer-Lambert law A = eps c l links absorbance to concentration.

Photoelectrochemistry uses light to create charge carriers. The band gap follows Eg(eV) = 1240/lambda(nm), and light below the threshold wavelength cannot drive the reaction. Electrogenerated chemiluminescence emits light from an excited state made electrochemically.

questions.question: Use the Beer-Lambert law A = eps c l. Calculate the absorbance for eps = 1.0e4 M-1 cm-1, c = 1.0e-4 M and l = 1.0 cm.
questions.explanation: A = 1.0e4 x 1.0e-4 x 1.0 = 1.0. Spectroelectrochemistry uses this to follow the concentration of a species as it is generated.

questions.question: The band gap of a semiconductor is related to wavelength by Eg(eV) = 1240/lambda(nm). Calculate Eg in eV for light of wavelength 620 nm.
For a semiconductor with a band gap of 2.0 eV, calculate the threshold wavelength in nm. (lambda = 1240/Eg.)
questions.explanation: lambda = 1240/2.0 = 620 nm. Light of longer wavelength has too little energy to create electron-hole pairs.

questions.question: In thin-layer spectroelectrochemistry the charge passed for 1.00e-4 mol is 19.30 mC. Calculate the number of electrons n (n = Q/(F x moles), F = 96485 C/mol).
The main advantage of in-situ spectroelectrochemistry is that it:
options: Identifies species optically while the electrode reaction is happening
Removes the need for a reference electrode
questions.explanation: By coupling the electrochemical cell to a spectrometer, the species formed at the electrode are identified in real time by their spectra, linking current to structure.

questions.question: In a photoelectrochemical cell, light with energy greater than the band gap can generate charge carriers that drive an electrode reaction.
questions.explanation: Absorbed photons with energy above the band gap create electron-hole pairs, which can separate at the semiconductor-solution junction and drive chemistry such as water splitting.

questions.question: Electrogenerated chemiluminescence (ECL) is:
options: Light emitted when electrochemically generated species react to form an excited state
questions.explanation: In ECL an electrode reaction produces radicals that react to form an excited molecule, which emits light. It is used in sensitive bioassays.

questions.question: A rotating ring-disk electrode lets the products formed at the disk be detected at the ring.
questions.explanation: Products generated at the disk are swept outward to the ring by the rotation, where they are detected electrochemically; the collection efficiency reports on intermediate stability.

questions.question: Which phenomena belong to spectroelectrochemistry or photoelectrochemistry? Select all that apply.
options: Diffusion-limited steady-state currents at a microelectrode
questions.explanation: In-situ optical monitoring, semiconductor photocurrents and ECL all involve light coupled to electrochemistry. A microelectrode steady-state current is a pure transport phenomenon with no light involved.

questions.question: Use A = eps c l. Calculate the absorbance for eps = 5.0e3 M-1 cm-1, c = 2.0e-4 M, l = 1.0 cm.
Calculate the band gap in eV for a semiconductor that absorbs light of wavelength 500 nm (Eg = 1240/lambda).
The rotating ring-disk electrode is used to:
options: Detect products formed at the disk by oxidising or reducing them at the ring
questions.explanation: Products generated at the disk are swept to the ring, where they are detected; the ring current reveals the fate and stability of reaction intermediates.

questions.question: A semiconductor electrode needs light with photon energy greater than its band gap to generate a photocurrent.
questions.explanation: Only photons with energy above the band gap create electron-hole pairs, so there is a threshold wavelength beyond which no photocurrent flows.

questions.question: Which are advantages of spectroelectrochemical techniques? Select all that apply.
options: Real-time observation of species during reaction
Measurement of the number of electrons from the charge
Elimination of the need for any electrode
questions.explanation: In-situ optics identify products in real time while coulometry gives n. An electrode is still required to drive the reaction.
